question: Who among the following was the Nizam of Hyderabad in 1947?
solution:
The correct answer is __Osman Ali__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seven Nizams, who were also known as Asaf Jahis, ruled Hyderabad – the seventh, Asaf Jah Nawab Mir Osman Ali Khan Bahadur reigned till 1948**__.

 __
 
• From 1724 to 1948, Hyderabad underwent immense growth, both culturally and economically.
 
• The Nizam chose not to join the Indian Union after India gained independence in August 1947.
 
• However, his rule ended in September 1948, when the Indian Army launched Operation Polo under the leadership of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the then Home Minister and Deputy Prime Minister of India.
 
• The State of Hyderabad was invaded and the Nizam was forced to step down.
 
• The Asaf Jahis were allowed to keep their titles even after their reign ended.
 
• Asaf Jah VII chose his grandson Nawab Mir Barakat Ali Khan Bahadur Mukarram Jah as his successor, but he was Nizam only in name.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nasir Jung**

 
 
• Mir Ahmed Ali Khan Siddiqi Bayafandi, Nasir Jung, was the son of Nizam-ul-Mulk by his wife Saeed-un-Nisa Begum.
 
• He was born on 26 February 1712. He succeeded his father as the Nizam of Hyderabad State in 1748.
 
• He had taken up a title of Humayun Jah, Nizam ud-Daula, Nawab Mir Ahmad Ali Khan Siddiqi Bahadur, Nasir Jung, Nawab Subadar of the Deccan. However, he is most famously known as **Nasir Jung.**
 
• The Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah bestowed him with the title Nasir Jung and later the next Mughal Emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur appointed him as the Subedar of the Deccan and bestowed him with the title Nasir-ud-Daula.
 
• **His official name was Humayun, Nizam ud-Daula, Nawab Mir Ahmad Ali Khan Siddiqi Bayafandi Bahadur, Nasir Jang, Nawab Subadar of the Deccan.**
 
• He ruled Hyderabad State in India from 1 June 1748 to 1750.
 
 
• He was appointed as his father's Deputy during his absence in Delhi from 1737 to 1741.
 
• In 1741 he attempted to seize power but was defeated by his father at the Eid Gah Maidan in Aurangabad, on 23 July 1741.
 
• After his father's death, he ascended the throne on 2 June 1748 at Burhanpur.
